questions.q: Let $f: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$~be a function defined as $f\left(x\right) = asin \left(\dfrac{\pi  \left[x\right]}${2}\right) + \left[2 - x\right], a \in \mathbb{R},$where~\left[t\right]$ is the greatest integer less than or equal to $t$. If $\lim_{x \to - 1}f  \left(x\right)$~exists, then the value of ${∫}_{0}^{4}f\left(x\right)dx$& is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$f\left(x\right) = asin\left(\dfrac{\pi\left[x\right]}{2}\right) + \left[2 - x\right], a \in \mathbb{R}$

Now given~$\lim_{x \to - 1}f\left(x\right)$~exists,

So~$\lim_{x \to - {1}^{+}}asin\left(\pi\left[x\right]2\right) + \left[2 - x\right] = - a + 2$

And~$\lim_{x \to - {1}^{-}} asin \left(\pi \left[$x\right]2\right) + \left[$2 - x\right] = 0 + 3 = 3$

So,~$\lim_{x \to - 1}f\left($x\right)$~exist when~$- a + 2 = 3 ⇒ a = - 1$

Now,

${∫}_{0}^{4}f\left($x\right)dx = {∫}_{0}^{1}f\left($x\right)dx + {∫}_{1}^{2}f\left($x\right)dx + {∫}_{2}^{3}f\left($x\right)dx + {∫}_{3}^{4}f\left($x\right)dx$

$⇒ {∫}_{0}^{4}f\left($x\right)dx = {∫}_{0}^{1} - sin\left(\dfrac{\pi\left[x\right]}{2}\right) + \left[$2 - x\right]dx + {∫}_{1}^{2} - sin\left(\dfrac{\pi\left[x\right]}{2}\right) + \left[$2 - x\right]dx + {∫}_{2}^{3} - sin\left(\dfrac{\pi\left[x\right]}{2}\right) + \left[$2 - x\right]dx + {∫}_{3}^{4} - sin\left(\dfrac{\pi\left[x\right]}{2}\right) + \left[$2 - x\right]dx$

$= {∫}_{0}^{1}\left($0 + 1\right)dx + {∫}_{1}^{2}\left(-$1 + 0\right)dx + {∫}_{2}^{3}\left($0 - 1\right)dx + {∫}_{3}^{4}\left($1 - 2\right)dx$

$= 1 - 1 - 1 - 1 = - 2$

$

questions.q: $\lim_{x \to a}\dfrac{ \left($a + 2x\$right)\dfrac{1}{3} -\left(3x\$right)\dfrac{1}{3}}{  \left($3a + x\$right)\dfrac{1}{3} -\left($4x\$right)\d$dfrac{1}{3}}\left($a \ne 0\right)$ \text{ and } is equal to:$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
At $x = a$, limit is of $\dfrac{0}{0}$~form.

So, applying L'Hospital rule, we get

$\lim_{x \to a}\dfrac{\left(a + 2x\right)\dfrac{1}{3} - \left(3x\right)\dfrac{1}{3}}{\left(3a + x\right)\dfrac{1}{3} - \left(4x\right)\dfrac{1}{3}} = \lim_{x \to a}\dfrac{\dfrac{1}{3}\left(a + 2x\right)- \dfrac{2}{3} . 2 - \dfrac{1}{3} . \left(3x\right)- \dfrac{2}{3} . 3}{\dfrac{1}{3}\left(3a + x\right)- \dfrac{2}{3} . - \dfrac{1}{3} . \left(4x\right)- \dfrac{2}{3} . 4}$

$= \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{3}\left(3a\right)- \dfrac{2}{3} . \left(2 - 3\right)}{\dfrac{1}{3}\left(4a\right)- \dfrac{2}{3} . \left(1 - 4\right)} = \dfrac{3- \dfrac{2}{3}}{4- \dfrac{2}{3}} . \dfrac{1}{3}$

$= \dfrac{2\dfrac{4}{3}}{9\dfrac{1}{3}} . \dfrac{1}{3} = \left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right)\left(\dfrac{2}{9}\right)\dfrac{1}{3}$

questions.q: Let $f, g$ and $h$ be the real valued functions defined on~$\mathbb{R}$ as $f\left(x\right) = \left\{\begin{cases}x\left|x\right|, & x \ne 0 \\ 1, & x = 0\end{cases}\right, g\left(x\right) = \left\{\begin{cases}sin\left(x + 1\right)\left(x + 1\right), & x \ne - 1 \\ 1, & x = - 1\end{cases}\right$and $h \left(x\right) = 2  \left[$x\right] - f \left(x\right)$,~where  \left[x\right]$ is the greatest integer $\lex$. Then the value of $\lim_{x \to 1}g \left(h  \left($x - 1\right)\right)$ is$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

Function& $f\left(x\right) = \left\{\begin{cases}x\left|x\right|, & x \ne 0 \\ 1, & x = 0\end{cases}\right, g\left(x\right) = \left\{\begin{cases}sin\left(x + 1\right)\left(x + 1\right), & x \ne - 1 \\ 1, & x = - 1\end{cases}\right$~and~$h \left(x\right) = 2 \left[$x\right] - f \left(x\right)$

To find~$\lim_{x \to 1}g \left(h \left(x - 1\right)\right)$

Taking~$L . H . L$,~we take~$x = 1 - h$

$\lim_{h \to {0}^{-}}g ( h ( 1 - h - 1 ) )$

$⇒ \lim_{h \to {0}^{-}}g \left($2 \left[-$h\right] - - h \left|-$h\right|\right)$

$⇒ \lim_{h \to {0}^{-}}g ( 2 ( - 1 ) + 1 )$

$⇒ \lim_{h \to ${0}^{-}}g\left(-$1\right) = 1$

Now taking~$R . H . L$,~we take~$x = 1 + h$

$\lim_{h \to {0}^{+}}g ( h ( 1 + h - 1 ) )$

$= \lim_{h \to {0}^{+}}g \left($2 \left[$h\right] - f ( h )\right)$

$= \lim_{h \to {0}^{+}}g ( 0 - 1 )$

$⇒ \lim_{h \to {0}^{+}}1 = 1$

questions.q: $\lim_{n \to \infty}\left(1 + \dfrac{1 + \dfrac{1}{2} + \ldots \ldots + \dfrac{1}{n}}{n2}\right)n$ is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
It is ${1}^{∞}$ form

$L = e^{\lim_{n \to \infty}\left(\left1 + \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{3} + \ldots . . + \dfrac{1}{n}\right)n\right)}$

$L = e^{\lim_{n \to \infty}\left(\dfrac{1}{n} + \dfrac{1}{2n} + \dfrac{1}{3n} + \ldots . . + \dfrac{1}{n2}\right)}$

$∴ L = e \left(0 + 0 + 0 + \ldots . . + 0\right)$

$⇒ L = e^{0} = 1

$

questions.q:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : $\lim _{x \rightarrow 0}\left(\frac{\tan ^{-1} x+\log _e \sqrt{\frac{1+x}{1-x}}-2 x}{x^5}\right)=\frac{2}{5}$
Statement II : $\lim _{\mathrm{x} \rightarrow 1}\left(\mathrmx^{\frac{2}{1-\mathrm{x}}}\right)=\frac{1}{\mathrm{e}^2}$
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{\tan ^{-1} x+\frac{1}{2}[\ln (1+x)-\ln (1-x)]-2 x}{x^5} \\ & =\lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{\left(x-\frac{x^3}{3}+\frac{x^5}{5} \ldots\right)+\frac{1}{2}\left[x-\frac{x^2}{2}+\frac{x^3}{3} \ldots-\left(-x-\frac{x^2}{2}-\frac{x^3}{3} \ldots\right)\right]-2 x}{x^5} \\ & =\lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{2 x+\frac{2 x^5}{5} \ldots-2 x}{x^5}=\frac{2}{5} \\ & \lim _{x \rightarrow 1} x^{\frac{2}{(1-x)}}=e^{\lim _{x \rightarrow l}\left(\frac{2}{(1-x)}\right)(x-1)}=e^{-2}
\end{aligned}$
\Rightarrow Both statements correct

questions.q: If $\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{3 + \alphasinx + \betacosx + \log_{\mathrm{e}} ( 1 - x )}{3\tan^{2}x} = \dfrac{1}{3}$, then $2\alpha - \beta$ is equal to :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{3 + \alpha sinx + \beta cosx + \log_{\mathrm{e}} ( 1 - x )}{3\tan^{2}x} = \dfrac{1}{3}$

$⇒ \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{3 + \alpha\left[x - \dfrac{x3}{3 !} + \ldots\right] + \beta\left[1 - \dfrac{x2}{2 !} + \dfrac{x4}{4 !} \ldots\right] + \left(- x - \dfrac{x2}{2} - \dfrac{x3}{3} \ldots\right)}{3\tan^{2}x} = \dfrac{1}{3}$

$⇒ \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{( 3 + \beta ) + ( \alpha - 1 ) x + \left(- \dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{β}{2}\right)x^{2} + \ldots .}{3x^{2}} \times \dfrac{x2}{\tan^{2}x} = \dfrac{1}{3}$

The coefficient of all the powers of $x$ except $x^{2}$ is $0$.

$⇒ \beta + 3 = 0, \alpha - 1 = 0$ and $\dfrac{- \dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{β}{2}}{3} = \dfrac{1}{3}$

$⇒ \beta = - 3, \alpha = 1$

$⇒ 2\alpha - \beta = 2 + 3 = 5$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given limits can be written as,

$⇒ 4 = \dfrac{3k^{2}}{2k}$
$⇒ k = \dfrac{8}{3}$.

questions.q: Let $f: \left[- \dfrac{π}{2}, \dfrac{π}{2}\right] \to R$ be a differentiable function such that $f\left(0\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}$, If $\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{x{∫}_{0}^{x}f ( t ) dt}{e^{x2} - 1} = \alpha$, then $8{α}^{2}$ is equal to :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let, $y = \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{x{∫}_{0}^{x}f ( t ) dt}{e^{x2} - 1}$

$⇒ y = \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{x{∫}_{0}^{x}f ( t ) dt}{\left(\dfrac{e^{x2} - 1}{x2}\right) \times x^{2}}$

We know that, $\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{e^{x2} - 1}{x2} = 1$

$⇒ y = \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{{∫}_{0}^{x}f ( t ) dt}{x}$

Applying L-hospital's rule and Newton Leibnitz Theorem we get,

$⇒ y = \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{f ( x )}{1}$

$⇒ y = f \left(0\right)$

It is given that, $f ( 0 ) = $\dfrac{1}{2}

$⇒ y = $\dfrac{1}{2}

$⇒ \alpha = $\dfrac{1}{2}

$⇒ 8{α}^{2} = 2

$

questions.q: If $\lim_{n \to \infty} \left(\sqrt{n^{2} - n - 1} +$+n\alpha + \beta\right) =$0$ then 8\left(\alpha + \beta\right)is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,& $\lim_{n \to \infty}\sqrt{n^{2} - n - 1} + \alphan + \beta = 0$

Now rewriting the expression we get,

$\lim_{n \to \infty}\left(n^{2} - n - 1\right)\dfrac{1}{2} + \alphan = - \beta$

$⇒\lim_{n \to \infty}n\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{n} - \dfrac{1}{n2}\right)\dfrac{1}{2} + \alphan = - \beta$

Now on using binomial approximation~\left(1 + x\right)n = 1 + nx$~we get,

$\lim_{n \to \infty}n\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{2n} - \dfrac{1}{2n^{2}}\right) + \alphan = - \beta$

$⇒ \lim_{n \to \infty}n - \dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2n} + \alphan = - \beta$

$⇒ \lim_{n \to \infty}n\left(1 + \alpha\right) - \dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2n} = - \beta$

Now for limit to exist~\left(1 + \alpha\right) = 0 ⇒ \alpha = - 1$

Now on putting the value of~$\alpha$~we get,

$\lim_{n \to \infty}n\left(1 + \alpha\right) - \dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2n} = - \beta$

$⇒ \lim_{n \to \infty} - \dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2n} = - \beta$

$⇒ - \dfrac{1}{2} - 0 = - \beta$

$⇒ \beta = \dfrac{1}{2}$

So,~$8\left(\alpha + \beta\right) = 8\left(- 1 + \dfrac{1}{2}\right) = 8 \times \dfrac{- 1}{2} = - 4$

questions.q: The value of& $\lim_{x \to {0}^{+}}\dfrac{\cos^{- 1}  \left(x - [ x{]}^{2}\$right)\cdot \sin^{- 1}\left(x - [ x{]}^{2}\right)}{x - x^{3}},$~where~\left[x\right]$~denotes the greatest integer~$\lex$ \text{ and } is:$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given& $L = \lim_{x \to {0}^{+}}\dfrac{\cos^{- 1}\left(x - [ x{]}^{2}\right) \cdot \sin^{- 1}\left(x - [ x{]}^{2}\right)}{x - x^{3}}$

$∵ x \in [ 0, 1 ) ⇒ \left[x\right] = 0$

Then~$L = \lim_{x \to {0}^{+}}\cos^{- 1}x\left(1 - x^{2}\right) \times \lim_{x \to {0}^{+}}\dfrac{\sin^{- 1}x}{x}$

$L = \dfrac{π}{2} \times \lim_{x \to {0}^{+}}\dfrac{1}{1 - x^{2}} \left(\text{Apply L'Hospital rule for}\dfrac{0}{0}\text{form}\right)

$L = \dfrac{π}{2}$

$

questions.q: The value of $\lim_{n \to \infty}\dfrac{\left[r\right] +  \left[2r\right] + . . . + \left[$nr\right]}{n2},$~where $r$~is non-zero real number and \left[$r\right]$ denotes the greatest integer less than or equal to $r,$& is equal to :$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We know that& $r \le \left[r\right] < r + 1$

$2r \le \left[2r\right] < 2r + 1$

$3r \le \left[3r\right] < 3r + 1$

$⋮ ⋮ ⋮$

$nr \le \left[nr\right] < nr + 1$

On adding all the above inequalities, we get

$r + 2r + \ldots + nr \le \left[r\right] + \left[2r\right] + . . . + \left[nr\right] < r + 2r + . . . nr + n$

Using~$1 + 2 + 3 + . . . + n = \dfrac{n\left(n + 1\right)}{2}, n \in N,$

$\dfrac{n\left(n + 1\right)}{2} \cdot r \le \left[r\right] + \left[2r\right] + . . . + \left[nr\right] < \dfrac{n\left(n + 1\right)}{2} \cdot r + n$

$⇒ \dfrac{\dfrac{n\left(n + 1\right)}{2} \cdot r}{n2} \le \dfrac{\left[r\right] + \left[2r\right] + . . . + \left[nr\right]}{n2} < \dfrac{\dfrac{n\left(n + 1\right)}{2} \cdot r + n}{n2}$

Now,~$\lim_{n \to \infty}\dfrac{n ( n + 1 ) \cdot r}{2 \cdot n^{2}} = \lim_{n \to \infty}\dfrac{n^{2}\left(1 + \dfrac{1}{n}\right) \cdot r}{2 \cdot n^{2}} = \dfrac{r}{2}$

and~$\lim_{n \to \infty}\dfrac{\dfrac{n\left(n + 1\right)}{2} \cdot r + n}{n2} = \lim_{n \to \infty}\dfrac{n^{2}\left\{\left(1 + \dfrac{1}{n}\right) \cdot r + \dfrac{1}{n}\right\}}{2 \cdot n^{2}} = \dfrac{r}{2}$

So, by Sandwich Theorem, we can conclude that

$\lim_{n \to \infty}\dfrac{\left[r\right] + \left[2r\right] + . . . + \left[nr\right]}{n2} = \dfrac{r}{2} .$

questions.q:
Let $f\left(x\right) = \left\{
x - 1, xis even,
2x, xis odd,
\rightx \in N$. If for some $a \in N, f\left(f\left(f\left(a\right)\right)\right) = 21$, then $\lim_{x \to a^{−}} \left\${\dfrac{ \left|$x\right|3}{a} - \left[\dfrac{x}{a}\right]\right\},$ where \left[t\right]$ denotes the greatest integer less than or equal to $t$, is equal to:$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given: $f\left(x\right) = \left\{
x - 1; xis even
2x: xis odd
\right$

And $f\left(f\left(f\left(a\right)\right)\right) = 21$

Case-I: If $a$ is even

$⇒ f\left(a\right) = a - 1 = \text{Odd}$

$⇒ f\left(f\left(a\right)\right) = 2\left(a - 1\right) = \text{Even}$

$⇒ f\left(f\left(f\left(a\right)\right)\right) = 2a - 3 = 21$

$⇒ a = 12$

Case-II: If $a$ is odd

$⇒ f\left(a\right) = 2a = \text{Even}$

$⇒ f\left(f\left(a\right)\right) = 2a - 1 = \text{Odd}$

$⇒ f\left(f\left(f\left(a\right)\right)\right) = 4a - 2 = 21$ (Not possible)

Hence, $a = 12$

Now,$\lim_{x \to {12}^{−}}\left(\dfrac{\left|x\right|3}{12} - \left[\dfrac{x}{12}\right]\right) = \lim_{x \to {12}^{−}}\dfrac{ \left|$x\right|3}{12} - \lim_{x \to {12}^{−}}\left[\dfrac{x}{12}\right]

$⇒ \lim_{x \to {12}^{−}}\left(\dfrac{\left|x\right|3}{12} - \left[\dfrac{x}{12}\right]\right) =$144 - 0$

$⇒ \lim_{x \to {12}^{−}}\left(\dfrac{\left|x\right|3}{12} - \left[\dfrac{x}{12}\right]\right) =$144$

questions.q:
The value of

$\lim_{n \to \infty}\dfrac{1 + 2 - 3 + 4 + 5 - 6 + \ldots + ( 3n - 2 ) + ( 3n - 1 ) - 3n}{\sqrt{2n^{4} + 4n + 3}-\sqrt{n^{4} + 5n + 4}}$& is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
The given limit& $\lim_{n \to \infty}\dfrac{1 + 2 - 3 + 4 + 5 - 6 + \ldots + ( 3n - 2 ) + ( 3n - 1 ) - 3n}{\sqrt{2n^{4} + 4n + 3}-\sqrt{n^{4} + 5n + 4}}$~can be expressed as,$\lim_{n \to \infty}\dfrac{\mathop{∑}_{r = 1}^{n}\left(3r - 2\right) + \left(3r - 1\right) - 3r}{\sqrt{2n^{4} + 4n + 3} - \sqrt{n^{4} + 5n + 4}}$

$= \lim_{n \to \infty}\dfrac{\mathop{∑}_{r = 1}^{n}3\left(r - 1\right)}{\sqrt{2n^{4} + 4n + 3} - \sqrt{n^{4} + 5n + 4}}$

$= \lim_{n \to \infty}\dfrac{0 + 3 + 6 + 9 + \ldots . nterms}{\sqrt{2n^{4} + 4n + 3} - \sqrt{n^{4} + 5n + 4}} . . . . . . . ( 1 )$

We know the sum of the nth term of A.P. is given by

${S}_{n} = \dfrac{n}{2} \left[2a + \left($n - 1\right)d\right]$

Using above formula in equation(1) we get,

$= \lim_{n \to $\$iinfty}\dfrac{3n ( n - 1 )}{2} \left(\sqrt{2n^{4} + 4n + 3} - \sqrt{n^{4} + 5n + 4}\right)$

~

$= \lim_{n \to $\$iinfty}\dfrac{3n ( n - 1 )}{2\$left(\sqrt{2n^{4} + 4n + 3} - \sqrt{n^{4} + 5n + 4}\right)}

$= \lim_{n \to $\iinfty}\dfrac{3 ( 1 - $\dfrac{1}{n} ))}{2 $\$left(\sqrt{2 + \dfrac{4}{n3} + \dfrac{3}{n4}} - \sqrt{1 + \dfrac{5}{n3} + \dfrac{4}{n4}}\right)}

$= $\dfrac{3 ( 1 - 0 )}{2\left(\sqrt{2 + 0 + 0} - \sqrt{1 + 0 + 0}\right)}

$= $\dfrac{3}{2 ( \sqrt{2} - 1 )} = \dfrac{3}{2} ( \sqrt{2} +$1 )$

questions.q: $\lim_{x \to \dfrac{\pi}{4}}\dfrac{8\sqrt{2} - {\left(cosx + sinx\right)}^{7}}{\sqrt{2} - \sqrt{2}sin2x}$ is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\lim_{x \to \dfrac{\pi}{4}}\dfrac{8\sqrt{2} - {\left(cosx + sinx\right)}^{7}}{\sqrt{2} - \sqrt{2}sin2x}\left(\dfrac{0}{0}form\right)$

$= \lim_{x \to \dfrac{\pi}{4}}\dfrac{- 7{\left(cosx + sinx\right)}^{6}\left(- sinx + cosx\right)}{- 2\sqrt{2}cos2x}$ (using L'Hospital Rule)

$= \lim_{x \to \dfrac{\pi}{4}}\dfrac{56\left(cosx - sinx\right)}{2\sqrt{2}cos2x}\left(\dfrac{0}{0}form\right)$

$= \lim_{x \to \dfrac{\pi}{4}}\dfrac{- 56\left(sinx + cosx\right)}{- 4\sqrt{2}sin2x}$ (using L'Hospital Rule)

$= \dfrac{56\sqrt{2}}{4\sqrt{2}} = 14$

$= \dfrac{56\sqrt{2}}{4\sqrt{2}} = 14$

questions.q: If& $\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{e^{ax} - cos ( bx ) - \dfrac{cxe^{- cx}}{2}}{1 - cos ( 2x )} = 17$, then $5a^{2} + b^{2}$& is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given that

$⇒ \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{e^{ax} - cos ( bx ) - \dfrac{cx}{2}e^{- cx}}{1 - cos2x} = 17$

We know that~$e^{ax} = 1 + ax + \dfrac{( ax{)}^{2}}{2 !} + \ldots$~and~$cos\left(bx\right) = 1 - \dfrac{( bx{)}^{2}}{2 !} + \ldots$

$⇒ \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{\left(1 + ax + \dfrac{\left(ax\right)2}{2 !} + \ldots\right) - \left(1 - \dfrac{\left(bx\right)2}{2 !} + \ldots\right) - \dfrac{cx}{2}\left(1 - \left(cx\right) + \dfrac{\left(cx\right)2}{2 !} - \ldots\right)}{\left(\dfrac{1 - cos2x}{\left(2x\right)2}\right) \times 4x^{2}} = 17$

$⇒ \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{\left(a - \dfrac{c}{2}\right)x + \left(\dfrac{a^{2} + b^{2} + c^{2}}{2}\right)x^{2} + \ldots}{\dfrac{1}{2} \times 4x^{2}} = 17$

Now for limit to exist,~$a - \dfrac{c}{2} = 0⇒ c = 2a$

$⇒ \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{\left(\dfrac{a^{2} + b^{2} + c^{2}}{2}\right)x^{2} + \ldots}{\dfrac{1}{2} \times 4x^{2}} = 17$

$⇒ \dfrac{a^{2} + b^{2} + c^{2}}{4} = 17$

$⇒ a^{2} + b^{2} + 4a^{2} = 68$

$⇒ 5a^{2} + b^{2} = 68$

Hence this is the correct option.

questions.q: For each $x \in R$, let  \left[x\right]$ be the greatest integer less than or equal to $x$. Then $\lim_{x \to {0}^{-}}x\left(\left[x\right] + \left|x\right|\right)sin ⁡ \left[x\right]\left|x\right|$ is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$= \lim_{x \to {0}^{-}} ⁡ \dfrac{x\left(\left[x\right] + \left|x\right|\right)sin ⁡ \left[x\right]}{\left|x\right|}$

$= \lim_{x \to {0}^{-}}\dfrac{x\left(- 1 - x\right)sin ⁡ \left(- 1\right)}{- x}$~ ~ ~\left\{\left[x\right] = - 1, ∀ x \in [ - 1, 0 )\right\}$

$= \lim_{x \to {0}^{-}} - \left(1 + x\right)sin ⁡ 1$~ ~ ~ ~\left\{sin\left(- \theta\right) = - sin\theta\right\}$

$= - sin ⁡ 1$.

questions.q: If the function $f(x)=\frac{\tan (\tan x)-\sin (\sin x)}{\tan x-\sin x}$ is continuous at $\mathrm{x}=0$, then $f(0)$ is equal to ________
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{\frac{\tan (\tan x)-\tan x}{\tan ^3 x} \frac{\tan ^3 x}{x^3}+\frac{\tan x-\sin x}{x^3}+\frac{\sin x-\sin (\sin x)}{\sin ^3 x} \frac{\sin ^3 x}{x^3}}{\frac{\tan x-\sin x}{x^3}}$
$=\frac{\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{6}}{\frac{1}{2}}=2$

questions.q: If $\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{ax - \left(e^{4x} - 1\right)}{ax\left(e^{4x} - 1\right)}$ exists and is equal to $b$, then the value of $a - 2b$ is ___ .
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{ax - \left($e^{4x} - 1\right)}{ax \left(e^{4x} - 1\right)}\left(\dfrac{0}{0}\right)$

$= \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{ax - \left(e^{4x} - 1\right)}{ax \cdot 4x}$~ Use~$\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{e^{4x} - 1}{4x} =1$

Apply $L$'Hospital Rule

$= \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{a - 4e^{4x}}{8ax}$~(~$\dfrac{a - 4}{0}$form )

limit exists only when $a - 4 = 0 ⇒ a = 4$

$= \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{4 - 4e^{4x}}{32x}$

$= \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{1 - e^{4x}}{8x} \$left(\dfrac{0}{0}\right)$

$= \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{-e^{4x} $\cdot$4}{8} = - \dfrac{1}{2}⇒ b = - \dfrac{1}{2}$

$a - 2b = 4 - 2 \left(- $\dfrac{1}{2}\right)

$= 5$

$

questions.q: $\lim_{x \to 0}\left(\dfrac{\left(x + 2cosx\right)3 + 2\left(x + 2cosx\right)2 + 3sin\left(x + 2cosx\right)}{\left(x + 2\right)3 + 2\left(x + 2\right)2 + 3sin\left(x + 2\right)}\right)\dfrac{100}{x}$& is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,$\lim_{x \to 0}\left(\dfrac{\left(x + 2cosx\right)3 + 2\left(x + 2cosx\right)2 + 3sin\left(x + 2cosx\right)}{\left(x + 2\right)3 + 2\left(x + 2\right)2 + 3sin\left(x + 2\right)}\right)\dfrac{100}{x}$

Now by putting the value of limit we can see it is in form~${1}^{∞}$

Now we know that,

$\lim_{x \to 0} \left(f \left($x\right)\right)g\left(x\right)$~when is in form of~${1}^{∞}$, we can write this as~$e^{\lim_{x \to $0}\$lleft(f\left($x\right) - 1\right)g\left(x\right)}$

Now using the above rule we get,

$= e^{\lim_{x \to 0}\left[\$left(\dfrac{\left($x + 2cosx\right)3 + $2\left($x + 2cosx\right)2 + 3sin \left(x + 2cosx\$right)}${\left($x + 2\right)3 + $2\left($x + 2\right)2 + $3sin\left($x + 2\right)}\right) -$1\right]\times $\dfrac{100}{x}}$

$= e^{\lim_{x \to 0}\$left[\dfrac{100}{x}\left[\dfrac{\left(x + 2cosx\right)3 + 2\left(x + 2cosx\right)2 + 3sin\left(x + 2cosx\right) - \left(\left(x + 2\right)3 + 2\left(x + 2\right)2 + 3sin \left($x + 2\right)\$right)}${\left($x + 2\right)3 + $2\left($x + 2\right)2 + $3sin\left($x + 2\right)}\right]\right]}$

$= e^{\lim_{x \to $0}\d$dfrac{100}{x}\left[\left(\dfrac{\left(x + 2cosx\right)3 - \left(x + 2\right)3 + 2\left(x + 2cosx\right)2 - 2 \left(x + 2\right)2 + 3sin\left(x + 2cosx\right) - 3sin\left(x + 2\right)}${8 + 8 + 3sin2}\right)\right]}$

Using L-hospital method we get,

$= e^{\dfrac{100}{16 + 3sin2}\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{3\left(x + 2cosx\right)2 \times \left(1 + 2sinx\right) - 3\left(x + 2\right)2 + 4\left(x + 2cosx\right) \times \left(1 - 2sinx\right) - 4\left(x + 2\right) + 3cos\left(x + 2cosx\right) \times \left(1 - 2sinx\right) - 3cos\left(x + 2\right)}{1}}$

$= e^{\dfrac{100}{16 + 3sin2} $\$left(\dfrac{12 - 3 \left(4\right) + 8 \times 1 - 8 + 3cos2 - 3cos2}${1}\right)}$

$= e^{\dfrac{100}{16 + 3sin2} \times$0}

$= e^{0} = 1$

questions.q: Let [t] be the greatest integer less than or equal to t. Then the least value of \($\mathrm{p} \in \mathbf{N}$\) for which \($\lim _{x \rightarrow 0^{+}}\left($x\left(\left[\frac{1}{x}\right]+\left[\frac{2}{x}\right]+\ldots+\left[\frac{\mathrm{p}}{x}\right]\right)-$x^2\left(\left[\frac{1}{x^2}\right]+\left[\frac{2^2}{x^2}\right]+\ldots+\left[\frac{9^2}{x^2}\right]\right)\right) \geq$1\) is equal to ________.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \lim _{x \rightarrow 0^{+}}\left(x\left(\left[\frac{1}{x}\right]+\left[\frac{2}{x}\right]+\ldots . .+\left[\frac{p}{x}\right]\right)-x^2\left(\left[\frac{1}{x^2}\right]+\left[\frac{2^2}{x^2}\right]+\left[\frac{9^2}{x^2}\right]\right)\right) \geq 1 \\ & \quad(1+2+\ldots \ldots+p)-\left(1^2+2^2+\ldots 9^2\right) \geq 1\end{aligned}\begin{aligned}
& \frac{p(p+1)}{2}-\frac{9.10 .19}{6} \geq 1 \\
& p(p+1) \geq 572
\end{aligned}$ Least natural value of $p$ is 24
